why: Almost everything is exact text, and the brief checked it against the code: the five names exist where it says, D366 to D573 sit at lines 708 to 904, and there are 12 open and 93 ticked PSI items, 17 long rows and the CLAUDE.md byte figure. Two parts can pass their checks and still do harm. scripts/claim-decision.mjs builds a commit with git plumbing (a temporary GIT_INDEX_FILE, commit-tree) and pushes it to main for real in commit 6, and only its pure part is unit-tested. Commit 4 hand-moves 17 tracker notes and 12 PSI items and re-wraps them, and the checks count rows, lines and items but not words, so a dropped or reworded sentence passes.
harm_if_wrong: A claim script that forgets the temporary index or reads the wrong base could push a commit to main that rewrites docs/decisions.md or disturbs the session's own index, and a careless re-wrap could silently drop facts from the code review's notes or the open PSI items.
make_it_cheaper: Add to claim-decision.test.ts a case that runs the script's git io against a bare repository and a clone made in os.tmpdir() (one commit holding docs/decisions.md) and checks the pushed commit changes only that file and leaves the clone's index and working tree untouched, and add to commit 4 a check that the sorted word list of each edited tracker is unchanged apart from the added 'see Notes below' and headings.
brief_problems: Commit 1 is told to edit src/lib/docs-budget.scan.test.ts, which does not exist until step 0.43 lands (the brief says so and stops if it is missing, so this step cannot start before 0.43).

The CLAUDE.md replacement for 'the last three bullets' is quoted from today's file and sized to -1 bytes; any earlier step that edits those bullets or adds a line makes the exact-text edit and the size check fail (stop_if covers it, but the step is fragile to ordering).
